findings.summary: HTML serialiser emits & raw instead of &, so escaped text re-parses as live markup
findings.description:
## Affected `github.com/malcolmston/puppeteer` **<= 0.2.0** (all published versions). No fix released. Parity cases: `parse-full-document`, `http-page-html` (harness finding IDs **P9** and **H2** in `parity/puppeteer/COVERAGE.md`). Oracle: `cheerio@1.0.0` (parse5 + dom-serializer). Affected output paths, all sharing one root cause in the serialiser: `Page.HTML()`, `Page.NormalizedHTML()`, `Element.OuterHTML()`, `Element.InnerHTML()`. ## Upstream vs port The serialiser does not escape `&` when writing text nodes back out. Parsing is correct - the text node holds the decoded value; the **encoder** loses the escaping. Given source `Doc & Title`: | | re-serialised | | --- | --- | | upstream (cheerio 1.0.0 / parse5) | `Doc & Title` - the `&` is re-escaped, round-trip is stable | | this port | `Doc & Title` - raw `&` | ## Impact (attacker terms) Serialisation is the boundary where text becomes markup again. Emitting `&` raw means text is emitted as markup, so the output of `Page.HTML()` is not safe to hand to anything that parses HTML - a template, a cache, a proxy, a browser. Content that was **inert escaped text in the source document comes back out live**: a source page containing the *text* `<script>alert(1)</script>` parses to the text node ``, and serialising without re-escaping produces a document in which that script executes. A scrape -> cache -> render pipeline built on `Page.HTML()` therefore converts harmless escaped user content on a third-party page into live script in its own output, letting whoever controls that page's user content inject script into the consumer's origin. URLs are corrupted the same way: `?a=1&b=2` re-serialises as `?a=1&b=2` in an `href`, and `&copy=1` re-parses as `©=1`. Round-tripping twice is not idempotent, the usual signature of an unsafe serialiser. Impact is contingent on the consuming application rendering or forwarding the serialiser output as HTML - which is the normal use of the API, but it is one step removed from direct script execution. ## Reproduction ```go const src = `Doc & Title` + `

<script>alert(1)</script>

` srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8") fmt.Fprint(w, src) })) defer srv.Close() b, _ := puppeteer.Launch(puppeteer.LaunchOptions{}) p, _ := b.NewPage() p.Goto(srv.URL) fmt.Println(p.HTML()) ``` Observed - the escaped `

``` Expected (what parse5/cheerio produces): ``` Doc & Title

<script>alert(1)</script>

``` ## Suggested fix In the text-node branch of the serialiser, escape per the HTML fragment serialisation algorithm: `&` -> `&`, `<` -> `<`, `>` -> `>`, U+00A0 -> ` `; in attribute values additionally `"` -> `"`. Escape `&` **first**, or the replacement's own ampersands get double-escaped. Raw-text elements (`script`, `style`) must stay verbatim, but `textarea` and `title` are RCDATA and must be escaped (a related bug tracked separately). ## Severity rationale Graded **medium** (CVSS-style "moderate"): a genuine port-specific defect (upstream escapes correctly) that can turn inert third-party text into executing script, but only once the consuming application renders the serialiser output as HTML, and the injected content must already be present as escaped text in a page the attacker influences. No impact on the library process itself.
